changed.title: With the ordered pair and triple witness conditions, selecting a row after free column preprocessing needs 2n−1 AND/OR gates
changed.statement:
∀ (n m p : Nat) (G : Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (code : Fin m → Fin p → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  2 ≤ n →
  (∀ u v : Fin n, u ≠ v →
    ∃ c : Fin m, G u c = true ∧ G v c = false) →
  (∀ u v w : Fin n, u ≠ v → u ≠ w → v ≠ w →
    ∃ c : Fin m, G u c = true ∧ G v c = true ∧ G w c = false) →
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C →
  (∀ (u : Fin n) (c : Fin m),
    C.eval (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => decide (i = u)) ++ List.ofFn (code c)) = G u c) →
  2 * n - 1 ≤ C.size
changed.unlocks: bounds the remaining row-selector gates when column preprocessing is free
changed.context: Fix the column code when comparing rows. With two incomparable rows both raw inputs matter and neither can feed the output directly. One shared initial gate treats them alike, so three gates are needed. Turning off a row saves two gates if it has two readers or its sole reader is AND. Otherwise count the private row ORs. Domination excludes a shared sole OR reader. A common column missed by a third excludes a shared sole AND reader. Charge two reader slots per row OR. The matching ceiling uses n free column predicates, n ANDs and n−1 ORs.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 101815 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 9 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (101815 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 9
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 10 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 9; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 2. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: Res(⊕) on the pigeonhole formula with 4 pigeons and 3 holes: some refutation has at most 51 lines
changed.statement: ∃ π : List (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.LinClause (Fin 4 × Fin 3)), PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsLinRefutation (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PHP 4 3) π ∧ π.length ≤ 51
changed.unlocks: one entry on the least length of a refutation of a small pigeonhole formula in resolution over linear equations modulo two: exact proof sizes in small, the ground for running proof search exactly
changed.context: SKETCH: truth not known to us; the opposite row is offered beside it. Proved by exhibiting ONE refutation with at most the stated number of lines: a list of linear clauses, each an axiom of the formula, a weakening of an earlier line, or the resolvent of two earlier lines on a linear form, ending in the empty clause; checked line by line. Our shortest refutation has one line more (computed, not checked), found by search and not by exhaustion. Size: minutes if such a refutation exists. No sorry, no new axiom. Own namespace for every declaration.
